stories.text: Gedling's railway station closed on 4 April 1960, though coal trains ran to the colliery for decades more. Its building is now a youth centre, and there are plans to reopen the line or make it a cycleway.

260511.sum: Gedling and Carlton railway station was a former railway station built to serve the villages of Gedling and Carlton in Nottinghamshire.

264144.today: The Parish Church of All Hallows

stories.text: All Hallows Church dates from the 13th century. It was restored in 1872, and its roof in 1892 by Arthur Blomfield. Its tall, thin broach spire has two tiers of lucarnes and a weathercock, and the church is listed Grade I.

264144.sum: All Hallows Church, Gedling, on Arnold Lane. Today it houses The Parish Church of All Hallows. The building was built in 1089, according to OpenStreetMap, though other sources give a different date. It is Grade I listed as Church of All Hallows.
